item.title: African Stablecoin Payments Startup Yellow Card Acquires Brazilian Crypto Firm GoMoney
item.dc:creator: WT Data Labs
item.description:
Yellow Card, an Africa-founded stablecoin payments infrastructure provider, has acquired Brazilian virtual asset

The post African Stablecoin Payments Startup Yellow Card Acquires Brazilian Crypto Firm GoMoney appeared first on WeeTracker.
item.content:encoded:
Yellow Card, an Africa-founded stablecoin payments infrastructure provider, has acquired Brazilian virtual asset service provider GoMoney, giving it a locally established operation in Latin America’s largest cryptocurrency market. The deal, completed in October 2026, was announced on Wednesday, with financial terms undisclosed.

Founded in São Paulo in 2018, GoMoney provides stablecoin-based cross-border payment services and will operate as a wholly owned Yellow Card subsidiary, retaining its founders and leadership.

Its acquisition gives Yellow Card access to local real-denominated collections and payouts through Brazil’s Pix payment system, with stablecoin settlement. GoMoney has applied for authorisation from Brazil’s central bank under the country’s new virtual asset regulatory framework.

item.title: Moroccan Adtech Startup Journify Raises USD 12 M Series A
item.dc:creator: WT Data Labs
item.description:
Journify, a Moroccan-founded advertising technology startup, has raised USD 12 M in a

The post Moroccan Adtech Startup Journify Raises USD 12 M Series A appeared first on WeeTracker.
item.content:encoded:
Journify, a Moroccan-founded advertising technology startup, has raised USD 12 M in a Series A round at four times its previous valuation to expand into the US and Europe and strengthen its artificial intelligence capabilities.

The round was led by Morocco’s Al Mada Ventures and co-led by returning investor Silicon Badia, with participation from existing investors Shorooq and Bunat Ventures, alongside new investors Du Ventures and Oraseya Capital.

Founded in 2022 by Taoufik El Jamali, Amine Chouki and Omar Al Shoubaki, Journify provides ad signal infrastructure that helps businesses collect, validate and securely transmit customer conversion data to advertising platforms including Google, Meta, TikTok, Snap and Amazon Ads.

Headquartered in San Francisco and Morocco, the company serves more than 100 businesses and has offices in Dubai and Riyadh.

item.title: Nigeria’s Helium Health Secures USD 2.5 M Google.org Grant For AI Maternal Care
item.dc:creator: WT Data Labs
item.description:
Helium Health, a Nigerian healthtech startup founded in 2014, has secured a NGN

The post Nigeria’s Helium Health Secures USD 2.5 M Google.org Grant For AI Maternal Care appeared first on WeeTracker.
item.content:encoded:
Helium Health, a Nigerian healthtech startup founded in 2014, has secured a NGN 3.4 B (USD 2.5 M) grant from Google.org to deploy artificial intelligence tools aimed at identifying pregnancy risks and improving maternal healthcare delivery in Nigeria.

The funding will support HeliumMum, the company’s maternal health initiative, which targets 1.9 million pregnant women over three years, beginning in Lagos before expanding to Delta, Kano and Oyo states.

Co-founded by Adegoke Olubusi, Dimeji Sofowora and Tito Ovia, Helium Health develops electronic medical records, hospital management and healthcare financing software.

Its new initiative will combine AI-powered risk detection with clinical decision-support tools to help community health workers identify pregnancy complications earlier. The company says its previous maternal health programmes have reached more than 3.5 million women.

item.title: KrosAI Raises USD 135 K To Expand AI Voice Infrastructure Across Africa
item.dc:creator: WT Data Labs
item.description:
KrosAI, an AI telecommunications infrastructure startup founded by Nigerian entrepreneur Joshua Barimon Firima,

The post KrosAI Raises USD 135 K To Expand AI Voice Infrastructure Across Africa appeared first on WeeTracker.
item.content:encoded:
KrosAI, an AI telecommunications infrastructure startup founded by Nigerian entrepreneur Joshua Barimon Firima, has raised USD 135 K to simplify the deployment of AI-powered voice agents across emerging markets.

The funding includes USD 60 K received through INSEAD’s AI Venture Lab, although the company has not disclosed the full breakdown of its investors.

Founded after Firima’s earlier AI venture encountered difficulties securing telecom partnerships and phone numbers, KrosAI connects AI voice agents to local telephone networks, handling phone number provisioning, identity verification and call routing.

The platform has established direct telecom connections in Nigeria and South Africa, attracted more than 60 paying businesses and processed hundreds of thousands of call minutes. It plans to expand into Rwanda and eventually operate in at least 15 countries.

item.title: SA Fintech CrissCross Secures Investment from Circle Ventures To Expand African Payments
item.dc:creator: WT Data Labs
item.description:
CrissCross, a South African cross-border payments company, has secured an undisclosed investment from

The post SA Fintech CrissCross Secures Investment from Circle Ventures To Expand African Payments appeared first on WeeTracker.
item.content:encoded:
CrissCross, a South African cross-border payments company, has secured an undisclosed investment from Circle Ventures, the investment arm of US-listed stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group, as it expands its payment infrastructure across Africa.

The investment was made through its parent company, Stitch Group, although neither party disclosed the amount or ownership stake involved.

CrissCross provides local collections, automated payouts, foreign exchange and corporate treasury services through a single API, connecting blockchain-based settlement with local bank accounts and mobile money wallets.

Its infrastructure supports more than 20 currencies across over 30 African markets, serving multinational companies, financial institutions and digital platforms. The investment will support the expansion of its stablecoin-powered payment infrastructure and strengthen its presence in African cross-border payment corridors.

item.title: Vitara Agritech Raises USD 2 M To Expand Ghana’s Shea Supply Chain
item.dc:creator: WT Data Labs
item.description:
Vitara Agritech, a Ghanaian agricultural technology company formerly known as Sommalife, has raised

The post Vitara Agritech Raises USD 2 M To Expand Ghana’s Shea Supply Chain appeared first on WeeTracker.
item.content:encoded:
Vitara Agritech, a Ghanaian agricultural technology company formerly known as Sommalife, has raised EUR 1.8 M (approximately USD 2 M) in early-stage equity funding to expand its digital sourcing infrastructure and strengthen its shea supply chain.

The round was led by the European Union-funded AgriFI facility, managed by EDFI Management Company, with participation from impact investor Acumen and private angel investors.

Co-founded by Mawuse Gyisun, Vitara uses its proprietary TreeSyt platform to track shea production, manage farmer networks and facilitate digital payments.

The company engaged 47,000 active women farmers during the 2025/2026 harvest season, with more than 150,000 producers registered on its platform. Women account for 91% of its smallholder collectors, whose household incomes have reportedly increased by 20% through its sourcing model.

item.title: Egypt’s Nclude VC Fund Reaches Final Close Above USD 112 M
item.dc:creator: WT Data Labs
item.description:
Nclude, an Egyptian fintech-focused venture capital fund launched in 2022, has reached a

The post Egypt’s Nclude VC Fund Reaches Final Close Above USD 112 M appeared first on WeeTracker.
item.content:encoded:
Nclude, an Egyptian fintech-focused venture capital fund launched in 2022, has reached a final close of more than USD 112 M as it prepares to expand investments across Africa and the Middle East.

The fund came under the management of Development Partners International (DPI) in 2025, with the firm acting as investment adviser through its dedicated DPI Venture Capital platform.

Nclude invests between USD 500 K and USD 10 M in startups from seed to Series C, focusing on fintech, financial inclusion and fintech-enabled businesses, including those applying AI and other emerging technologies.

Egypt remains its core market, although up to 30% of its investment mandate can be deployed elsewhere in the region. The fund has backed 15 companies to date, with its portfolio also extending into affordable insurance, healthcare access and SME credit.
